result.paraphrase: As next-generation passive optical network (PON) capacity moves toward 100 Gb/s and beyond, cost-effective transceivers have become a major topic of discussion. This work presents a detailed numerical-simulation comparison of simplified coherent and direct-detection (DD) schemes for a 100 Gb/s/λ 4-ary pulse-amplitude-modulation signal. Based on cost, coherent receivers are categorized into three tiers: intensity-only coherent receivers, and phase-insensitive and phase-sensitive complex-value coherent receivers. For each transceiver type, the study examines and analyzes back-to-back received-power sensitivity, the effects of laser frequency offset, local-oscillator power, laser linewidth, analog-to-digital converter resolution, fiber dispersion, and hardware complexity. The results indicate that (1) transmitter-side optical amplification is recommended for DD and intensity-only coherent receivers to satisfy the 29 dB power-budget requirement, though these schemes suffer a large dispersion penalty; (2) compared with 3×3-coupler- and 2×4-hybrid-based coherent receivers, 2×2-coupler and balanced-photodiode-based heterodyne detection delivers similar performance with a simpler structure; and (3) phase-insensitive and phase-sensitive complex-value coherent receivers both offer better power budget and dispersion tolerance, with their use in PON determined by cost.
